trust_decision.summary: The CustomVerbAuthorizer admission plugin decides whether a Project CREATE/UPDATE that changes .spec.members (and .spec.owner) must present the `manage-members` custom verb for the project; the decision is made by classifying each changed member subject through findHumanUsersWithRoles/isHumanUser, which at the pinned commit recognises only Kind=User (minus the serviceaccount name prefix) and therefore never sees Kind=Group subjects, so a group injection was never authorized.

landing_point.why: A reader of 'Authorization Bypass via Group Subject Injection' searches for the code that decides which subjects are protected; isHumanUser is the single place that enumerates the protected subject kinds, and it returns true only for Kind=User without the system:serviceaccount: prefix.

fix_sites.entry_point: gardener-apiserver admission: CREATE/UPDATE of core.gardener.cloud Project (Validate -> admitProjects -> mustCheckProjectMembers)
same admission check: the subject classifier isServiceAccountSubject (was isHumanUser) and memberSubjectKey used by findNonServiceAccountsWithRoles
fix_sites.module_kind: admission plugin helper (same package, lower-level predicate)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: ProjectMemberProperties/ProjectMemberId (used for duplicate detection and member identity in the registry validation) is a second, independently written subject classifier that takes no user info, so a solver can argue authorization cannot be enforced there and that the fix belongs only in the admission plugin.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Service-account members (Kind=ServiceAccount with empty APIGroup, and Kind=User named system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<name>) must stay addable/removable with the plain update/patch verbs without `manage-members`, and the auto-added owner entry in .spec.members must stay exempt from the check so that transferring .spec.owner does not require the `manage-members` verb; an over-broad fix that protects every subject breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: Kind=Group subject added, removed or re-roled in .spec.members (the main variant; previously invisible to the check)
Kind=ServiceAccount subject carrying a non-empty APIGroup (now treated as non-service-account, i.e. protected)
Kind=User subject whose name starts with system:serviceaccount: but whose APIGroup is not rbac.authorization.k8s.io (now treated as non-service-account, i.e. protected)
Kind=ServiceAccount subject with empty APIGroup (stays a service account, remains unprotected, must keep working)
Kind=User subject with the rbac API group and no serviceaccount prefix (unchanged, protected)
members with multiple roles / role-only changes, keyed as (member,role) pairs

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Project UPDATE that adds, removes or re-roles the owner subject's own entry in .spec.members: the owner key is deleted from both sides of the comparison before the decision, so a user holding only the plain update verb can modify the owner's membership without `manage-members`
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The code comment says the owner entry is removed 'to always allow it to be added' and the exemption is needed so that changing .spec.owner does not require the uam verb; a solver reads the comment as intent and leaves it alone
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Project UPDATE on a project whose .spec.owner is nil: userIsOwner returns true for every requester and mustCheckProjectMembers returns false, so any user with plain update can add/remove human and group members without `manage-members`
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The comment states owner==nil means 'the creator will be defaulted to the owner', and .spec.owner is documented as deprecated in favour of the owner role, so a solver calls the nil-owner state unsupported/legacy and out of scope
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different helper reached through the same call site

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A subject-identity normaliser in the validation package that must agree with the admission classifier (it already normalises system:serviceaccount: user names into service accounts).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The package already owns ProjectMemberProperties/ProjectMemberId for duplicate detection; a maintainer fixing subject handling would naturally add the same service-account/group normalisation there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A filter on the consumer side that refuses to render protected subject kinds into ClusterRoleBindings unless the member carries the uam role.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the code that turns .spec.members into project RBAC, the actual privilege sink, so a maintainer hardening group injection could add a guard here instead of, or in addition to, the admission plugin.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Subject/role normalisation at the conversion boundary (the owner role is injected into the matching member here by a different identity comparison than the admission key).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The conversion already mutates member roles based on a name+apiGroup+kind comparison, so a maintainer could plausibly put the group/service-account identity rule at this serialization boundary.

O9_family: authorization bypass (CWE-863): incomplete subject-kind classification in a Kubernetes admission plugin lets project admins/members grant project RBAC to groups without the manage-members verb
